ProofCheck/How it works
THE PROOFCHECK METHOD

Evidence gets a record, not a halo.

ProofCheck does one focused job in the MVP: evaluate public claims about whether a GitHub repository is open source.

01
WHAT WE CHECK

A claim must meet its sources.

For an open-source claim, validators look for a public repository, relevant implementation code, and a clear usable license. A public link by itself is not enough.

CHECK 01Public access

Can the submitted repository and evidence be reached?

CHECK 02Relevant source

Does the repo contain the implementation described?

CHECK 03Clear license

Is there a license that makes the open-source claim meaningful?

02 / THREE STATUSES

Neutral outcomes, clear meaning.

NO PERMANENT BADGES

Supported

The public evidence fits the wording of the claim at review time.

Evidence supports the statement.

Insufficient

Sources are missing, inaccessible, ambiguous, or not specific enough.

Do not fill gaps with assumptions.

Refuted

A source directly conflicts with the wording of the claim.

Evidence contradicts the statement.
03 / GENLAYER'S ROLE

Validators read. Consensus records.

ProofCheck's Intelligent Contract fetches the submitted web sources, asks validators to assess the evidence, and stores the decisive status with the review metadata.

01Web AccessFetch public sources
02Validator reviewCompare the status
03On-chain recordPreserve the result
free write submit_claim(claim_type, claim, repo, evidence) // 0 GEN verification fee on testnet
04 / THE BOUNDARY

What ProofCheck does not claim.

  • ×

    It does not know absolute truth.

  • ×

    It does not certify a project forever.

  • ×

    It does not erase a previous review when challenged.
